747581.rationale: Mercedes has won 6 of 7 races and taken every pole (Antonelli 5 wins, Russell 1); Hamilton won Barcelona for Ferrari via strategy/VSC. Shares follow Austria odds (Antonelli 2.75, Russell 3.5, Hamilton 5, Leclerc 7.5, Verstappen 11, Norris 13) with a small home boost for the British drivers.
747581.next_info: Austrian GP result Jun 28; Silverstone sprint weekend Jul 3-5 (sprint quali Jul 3, sprint + GP quali Jul 4); race-week odds.

556116.rationale: After round 7: Antonelli 156, Hamilton 115, Russell 106, Leclerc 75. Before Spa there are 3 GPs and 1 sprint (Austria, Britain incl. sprint, Belgium). A Monte Carlo using odds-based strengths gave Hamilton about 58% and Russell about 41% for 2nd. Shaded slightly toward Russell because Mercedes is the faster car.
556116.next_info: Austria Jun 28 and Silverstone Jul 4-5: recompute the gap after each and update sharply. Belgian GP Jul 19.

475441.rationale: Mercedes has every pole. In 2026 FP3, Antonelli topped Monaco and Russell topped Barcelona, where Piastri, Leclerc and Norris were within 0.25s. Leclerc is usually quicker than Hamilton over one lap. Hungary is not a sprint weekend, so FP3 is held (Jul 25).
475441.next_info: Pace at Austria/Silverstone/Spa; Hungary FP1/FP2 Jul 24 (strong signal); FP3 Jul 25.

918398.rationale: Bahrain and Saudi were dropped in March with no replacement (22 races). Options under review: reinstate Bahrain (FIA's preference, freight still there) or Saudi on Oct 2-4, or bring Turkey (Istanbul Park, which needs homologation) forward. Imola and Portimao were also floated. The question's wording about pending 'regulatory approval' fits the Istanbul homologation case. A US-Iran deal around Jun 24 makes reinstating Bahrain itself more plausible. There is a large chance of no announcement at all, which is not representable.
918398.next_info: Any F1/FIA calendar announcement, likely before the summer break (late July) or by August, given the Oct 2-4 slot; Middle East deal progress; Istanbul homologation news.

594916.rationale: Same odds-based baseline as Silverstone with slightly more spread for the time horizon. Qualifying matters at the Hungaroring, which favours Mercedes (all poles). McLaren (2024-25) and Leclerc (2025 pole) have been strong here before.
594916.next_info: Results of Austria (Jun 28), Britain (Jul 5), Belgium (Jul 19); Hungary FP/quali Jul 24-25; race Jul 26.

669987.rationale: Mercedes favourite under the current pecking order. Kept wider because development could move the order before the summer break. Zandvoort is a sprint weekend.
669987.next_info: Pre-summer-break races (Jun 28-Jul 26), post-break upgrades; Dutch GP Aug 21-23.

668636.rationale: Mercedes baseline. Antonelli is Italian and racing at home; Monza is Ferrari's home race and favours low drag, so Ferrari gets a small bump.
668636.next_info: Form through Zandvoort Aug 23; Monza weekend Sep 4-6.

48458.rationale: Madring is a new street/hybrid circuit with no track history. Uses the generic odds-based split with Mercedes favoured.
48458.next_info: Form through Monza Sep 6; Madrid weekend Sep 11-13.

447470.rationale: Mercedes baseline. Baku is a street circuit, where Russell is strong and Leclerc has a big qualifying record. Verstappen (2025 winner) and Piastri (2024) are tail risks. The race is on Saturday, Sep 26.
447470.next_info: Form through Madrid Sep 13; Baku weekend Sep 24-26.

315568.rationale: Alonso's contract ends in 2026. He will decide 'after summer' between staying, Alpine (Briatore and Gucci are pushing) and retiring. Aston Martin wants to keep him, and ESPN sources say many inside the team expect him to continue. Aston Martin is very uncompetitive (1 point), and a B-spec arrives at Spa. Reported fallbacks are Perez (contracted to Cadillac to 2027), Sainz, Tsunoda (Honda link) and long-shot elite names.
315568.next_info: Spa AMR26-B debut Jul 17-19; Alpine lineup decision before the summer break (Briatore: late July); Alonso decision after the summer break (late Aug-Sep); a likely AM announcement around Sep.

897546.rationale: Marquez has won the last two GPs (Balaton, Brno) after shoulder surgery in early May. Sachsenring is his strongest track: 9 MotoGP wins there including 2025. Aprilia (Bezzecchi 4 GP wins and the title lead; Martin 2nd) is considered the best bike overall.
897546.next_info: Assen Dutch TT Jun 26-28 (form/fitness); Sachsenring Jul 10-12.

259947.rationale: Silverstone suits Aprilia: Bezzecchi won there in 2025 and Aprilia is called the best bike. Marquez is resurgent but his Silverstone record is weaker. Bagnaia has 3 straight podiums, and Ogura took pole and 2nd at Brno.
259947.next_info: Assen Jun 28, Sachsenring Jul 12, Silverstone weekend Aug 7-9.

187330.rationale: Palou has 6 poles in 10 races, including 5 in a row (IMS road course, Indy 500, Detroit, WWT, Road America). On 2026 street courses, the new one-lap Fast Six format has produced 4 different polesitters (McLaughlin, Ericsson, Rosenqvist, Palou), with Palou top-4 every time. DC is a brand-new circuit.
187330.next_info: Mid-Ohio Jul 5, Nashville Jul 19, Portland Aug 9, Markham street race Aug 16 (best street-form signal); DC practice/qualifying Aug 21-22.
